input: Audience: Established wedding-business owners with reviews and testimonials who still lack clear evidence about the reasons couples chose them. | Tension: Reviews are visible and useful, but relying on them to explain purchase decisions may leave the business guessing about what mattered before a couple booked. | Argument: Positive reviews can document how a couple experienced a wedding, but they do not necessarily reveal what helped that couple choose the business. Owners who want stronger buyer-specific evidence for messaging can consider asking decision-focused questions after booking and preserving the answers for later review. | Take: Separate experience feedback from questions about the buying decision. If collecting post-booking answers, decide who will send the survey, how responses will be stored, and how they may inform messaging. | Mechanism: In an internal discussion, Whitney distinguished reviews about past experience from a proposed survey sent after a new client signs to investigate buying triggers. She outlined a possible LeadLock workflow in which the client would send or trigger the survey, responses would be available in a spreadsheet, and findings could be considered for ad copy and landing pages. | Reader decision: Decide whether existing reviews answer the specific question you have about why couples booked; if not, consider whether a repeatable post-booking survey is practical for your business.
